intro.title: Physical health and vitality calculator
intro.body: Enter a few simple details — height, weight, activity, sleep, and nutrition — and answer a short questionnaire. You get a vitality score, clear metrics, and small tips you can try. Everything stays in your browser. This is a tool for inspiration, not a substitute for medical advice.

setup.title: Background data and metrics
setup.subtitle: Straightforward numbers that help paint a picture — not a label.

activity.sedentary: Mostly sedentary — little or no exercise
activity.light: Light — once or twice a week

metrics.bmrHint: Basic estimate using a common formula
metrics.tdeeHint: Includes the activity level you chose

profiles.vital-steady: Steady vitality — a good base for daily life
profiles.mostly-vital: Mostly vital — with room to improve
profiles.solid-enough: Solid enough — you can gently pick up the pace
profiles.tired-edges: Running on tired — your body is asking for rest
profiles.one-habit-week: One habit this week is enough

insights.dim-energyBalance-high: Your daily energy looks fairly steady — food, water, and pace all help.
insights.dim-energyBalance-low: Energy runs out fast. Regular meals and water through the day make a big difference.
insights.dim-recoveryQuality-high: Recovery is working for you — sleep and rest support your body.
insights.dim-recoveryQuality-low: Your body isn’t recovering enough. An extra half hour of sleep often beats another workout.
insights.dim-activityRhythm-high: You have a good movement rhythm. Consistency matters more than going all out.
insights.dim-activityRhythm-low: Regular movement is missing. Ten minutes of walking most days beats a perfect plan that never happens.
insights.overall-strong: Overall your body gets good support — you can fine-tune without breaking your routine.
insights.overall-steady: A reasonable, human place — clear strengths and a few habits to strengthen.
insights.overall-developing: You’re aware, but the routine doesn’t hold everything yet. A small step beats a revolution.
insights.overall-needs-care: Your body is asking for ease and order. Start with one thing — sleep or gentle movement.
insights.bmi-under: Body mass is below the usual range. Make sure you’re eating enough — and talk to a professional if you need to.
insights.bmi-healthy: Body mass is in the usual range — a comfortable starting point, not the whole story on health.
insights.bmi-high: Body mass is above the usual range. Steady movement and eating help more than extreme diets.
insights.bmi-higher: Body mass is on the higher side. Small, consistent steps — and professional support if you can.
insights.sleep-short: Sleep is short for most people. It affects energy, mood, and recovery.
insights.sleep-fair: Sleep is almost enough — a little more can make a difference.
insights.sleep-good: Your sleep hours look good. Keep a consistent sleep window.
insights.sleep-long: Very long sleep — sometimes that’s fine, sometimes a sign of built-up fatigue.
insights.activity-sedentary: Little movement each week. Start small — stairs, walking, or stretching.
insights.activity-light: You have some light movement. Adding one fixed day can change how you feel.
insights.activity-regular: Regular activity — one of the strongest habits for health.
insights.activity-intense: High training load. Rest days and sleep matter just as much.
insights.nutrition-needsWork: Eating could use a boost. One balanced meal a day is a good start.
insights.nutrition-mixed: Mixed eating — good days and gaps. Small consistency wins.
insights.nutrition-mostlyGood: Most days your food supports you. Keep that up on busy days too.
insights.nutrition-strong: Steady eating — a great base for energy and recovery.

tips.tip-water-bottle: Keep a water bottle nearby today — three refills before evening.
tips.tip-protein-breakfast: Breakfast with protein (egg, yogurt, cheese) helps steady energy.
tips.tip-walk-after-lunch: Ten minutes of walking after a meal — easy and energizing.
tips.tip-earlier-bed: Go to bed twenty minutes earlier this week — no screens in bed.
tips.tip-screen-off: Turn off screens half an hour before sleep — helps you fall asleep faster.
tips.tip-rest-day: Plan one rest day this week — even if you feel you “should” train.
tips.tip-ten-minute-move: Ten minutes of movement today: walk, stretch, or take the stairs.
tips.tip-stairs-choice: Choose stairs over the elevator once a day — it counts.
tips.tip-calendar-workout: Block a short workout on your calendar like a meeting — then just show up.
tips.tip-weekly-check: Once a week: how are energy, sleep, and movement? One sentence only.
tips.tip-sleep-window: Set a steady sleep window for seven days — weekends included.
tips.tip-outdoor-light: Ten minutes of daylight in the morning — helps sleep rhythm and alertness.

daytime-energy.prompt: Midday I have enough energy to get through without crashing.

options.2: Most days very tired after noon
options.4: Most days I manage reasonably well
options.5: Steady energy for most of the day

water-habit.prompt: I drink enough water during the day — not just coffee.

options.4: Most days I drink a reasonable amount

afternoon-slump.prompt: An afternoon slump doesn’t shut me down completely.

options.3: There’s a slump but I can push through
options.4: Mild slump I know how to handle
options.5: Almost no slump — or I know how to prevent it

steady-meals.prompt: I don’t skip meals until hunger is extreme.

options.1: I regularly go long hours without eating
options.4: Most days I have a reasonable meal rhythm
options.5: I eat regularly even on busy days

wake-feeling.prompt: In the morning I wake up feeling ready to start the day.

bySleep.short: With my short sleep — I still manage to get up without feeling totally wrecked.
bySleep.fair: With my current sleep hours — mornings feel doable.
bySleep.good: With good sleep hours — I wake up relatively ready.
bySleep.long: Even after long sleep — I check whether mornings actually feel refreshed.

options.1: I wake up wrecked almost always
options.5: I wake up with fairly good energy

sore-recovery.prompt: After effort — my body recovers in a reasonable time.

byActivity.sedentary: Even after small effort (stairs, walking) — I’m not wiped out for days.
byActivity.light: After light activity — I bounce back without lasting soreness.
byActivity.intense: Between intense workouts — I give my body time to recover.

options.1: Pain or exhaustion lasts for days
options.4: Most of the time I’m back on track in time

rest-day-respect.prompt: I can give my body a rest day without guilt.

byActivity.sedentary: When you start moving — rest is part of the picture too, not failure.
byActivity.light: Between active days — there’s room to rest without pressure.
byActivity.regular: In a training routine — rest days are planned.
byActivity.intense: Even with a heavy load — rest is part of training.

options.2: Hard to rest even when I need it
options.4: Most of the time I honor rest

move-most-days.prompt: Most days of the week I get some movement — even if brief.

byActivity.sedentary: Even without a gym — there’s a little daily movement (walking, stairs).
byActivity.light: Beyond 1–2 workouts — there’s everyday light movement too.
byActivity.regular: Between regular workouts — I’m not fully sedentary.
byActivity.intense: Beyond training — a normal day still includes some movement.

options.2: Only when there’s a formal workout
options.5: Movement is a regular part of my routine

strength-feel.prompt: I feel I have basic physical strength for everyday tasks.

options.4: Most of the time I have reasonable strength
options.5: I feel strong and steady day to day

chronic-fatigue-edge.prompt: Ongoing fatigue doesn’t run my whole day.

options.1: Heavy fatigue almost all the time
options.3: Hard days and normal days mix
options.4: Fatigue is managed — it doesn’t take over
